They likely have the four blessings of working peacefully, supporting their family, that being spouses, parents, children, and other relatives too.
I think a protector or follower of the Dhamma.
He wanted to find out if young people really didn't die in the boy's village.

Long ago, there was a boy who went to study with a great teacher after coming of age and became an assistant after working hard. Soon after, the son of his teacher died at a young age, something nearly unheard of in the boy's home village. In shock of this revelation, the teacher decided to test this by visiting the boy's home with a bag of bones in his hands, to tell them their son died, although he was still young. The family then explained how this was impossible because of the good, moral lives they all led there, where people worked and lived peacefully, and honestly. These being the "secret" to a long life, the teacher wrote this down and noted it happily before returning.
I think the main lesson I learned was that living an honest, peaceful life, will lead to being able to live a long life.
One should live a life without doing anything rash and bad in general, being responsible for their actions and having good moral conduct.
I helped make and prepare food with my parents, and didn't cause any trouble for anyone and interacted peacefully.
I am most familiar with the first 3, being not to associate with bad people, befriending wise people and associating with them, and I believe the third one is honoring the wise.
According to the story, they didn't die young because they followed and protected the dhamma so much so that their village is named after this.
